model_type: Book-value compounding (BVPS growth x exit Price/Book) with dividend income, discounted at Cost of Equity -- NOT a free-cash-flow DCF

valuation_philosophy.methodology: Heartland Group Holdings is a dual-country bank holding company (Heartland Bank Limited, NZ registered bank; Heartland Bank Australia Limited, an APRA-regulated ADI). This model values the EQUITY DIRECTLY via book-value compounding: intrinsic value = PV of projected dividends per share (Years 1-5, FY27-FY31) + PV of a Year-5 exit value equal to projected Year-5 book value per share x an assumed exit Price-to-Book multiple, both discounted at Cost of Equity (CoE). This is the same family of model used elsewhere in this repo for depository/insurance institutions (GEN.NZ, SOFI, SRBK, FRFHF, FIH.U).
valuation_philosophy.why_not_fcf_dcf: FreeCashFlow is deliberately NULL in HGH.NZ_Metrics.csv and must stay that way. Reported operating cash flow for a growing bank is dominated by loan-book and deposit flows, not owner earnings: FY2024 OCF was +$928.4m (deposit inflows outpacing loan growth that year) while FY2021 OCF was -$339.5m (the mirror image) -- neither figure has any relationship to distributable value, both are pure funding-flow artefacts of balance-sheet timing. There is also no meaningful enterprise-value/net-debt bridge for a bank: TotalDebt in the CSV (wholesale borrowings only, NULL for the latest periods) is not comparable financing debt to net against equity, and customer deposits (~$6.53bn) are the funding base of the lending business, not debt -- no net-debt subtraction is applied anywhere in this model; the equity is valued directly.
valuation_philosophy.sbc_treatment: Stock-based compensation appears in the CSV as small positive/negative StockBasedComp-style noise embedded in reported NetIncome via LTI/STI accrual movements, but it is immaterial to a bank valuation built off ROE-on-book-value rather than owner FCF, and no separate SBC deduction or dilution adjustment is made -- book value already reflects the accounting cost of any equity-settled incentive schemes as they vest.
valuation_philosophy.tsb_merger_treatment: On 2 June 2026 Heartland announced a conditional agreement to acquire TSB Bank Limited from Toi Foundation for ~NZ$620m, creating 'TSB Heartland Bank' (NZ's 7th-largest bank, ~NZ$15bn total assets), targeted completion December 2026, funded via ~$250m new equity (approximately 200m new shares at $1.25), $56m subordinated debt and a $264m vendor loan from Toi Foundation. This is modelled explicitly, not ignored: (1) the $250m equity raise and ~200m new shares are added to the share count and book value at the start of FY27 in every scenario; (2) management's guidance of $34m annual run-rate synergies and >20% year-one EPS accretion is NOT taken at face value -- Heartland's LAST acquisition (the Australian ADI, completed April 2024) was followed by two years of underlying ROE below 8% (FY2025 underlying ROE only 4.2%) as integration costs ran hot and synergies were slower to land than guided. The base case therefore assumes underlying ROE DIPS to 6.5-7.0% in FY27-FY28 (echoing the AU integration pattern) before a partial, haircut recovery toward 8.5-9.0% by FY30-FY31 as roughly 60-70% of guided synergies are eventually realised, later than management's timeline. Bull assumes the deal executes cleanly on guidance with full synergies (ROE to 11% by FY31); bear assumes integration repeats the AU experience but worse, with ROE stuck at 6-6.5% throughout the horizon.
valuation_philosophy.roe_vs_coe: The central fact this valuation must confront: Heartland's underlying ROE has been persistently below a reasonable cost of equity for a small, dual-regulator, currently-integrating bank. FY2025 underlying ROE was 4.2% (reported 3.2%); FY2026 guidance floor is only >=7% underlying; 1H2026 underlying ROE recovered sharply to 7.3% but is still well below the ~13.1% cost of equity built up below. Under the standard justified-P/B identity, P/B = (ROE - g) / (CoE - g); with a medium-term steady-state ROE assumption of ~8.5%, sustainable growth g of ~3.8% (ROE x (1-55% payout)) and CoE 13.1%, the theoretically fair P/B is only ~0.50x -- materially BELOW the current ~0.88x traded multiple (bvps at H1-2026 of $1.3705 against the $1.205 quote) and below even this model's base-case discounted-cashflow-style output of 0.74x book. The market's current pricing therefore already embeds a meaningfully more optimistic ROE recovery than either the formula-fair or DCF-style base case here assumes -- it is pricing in the TSB synergy story and a return to Heartland's historical low-teens ROE ambition working out largely as guided. This model's base case does NOT assume that clean an outcome, given the AU integration precedent, and its base-case output is a MODEST DOWNSIDE (-15.7%) to the current price -- this is a deliberate, honest conclusion, not a modelling artefact. A materially positive base-case return would require assuming the TSB deal succeeds essentially as guided with limited integration drag, which is what the bull case (not base case) models.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Latest confirmed period-end share count is FY2025 (940.559m); H1-2026 (31-Dec-2025) share count is not separately disclosed in the CSV, so FY2025 is used as the pre-TSB-raise anchor for the H1-2026 book value per share calculation.
inputs.net_debt_note: Not applicable / not computed. Customer deposits (~$6.53bn) fund the lending business and are not financing debt to net against equity; wholesale borrowings (TotalDebt) are NULL for the latest periods in the CSV and immaterial to an equity-value model. No net-debt bridge is used anywhere in this model.
inputs.free_cash_flow_note: Deliberately NULL. Reported operating cash flow (FY2024 +$928.4m, FY2021 -$339.5m) reflects loan-book and deposit-flow timing, not owner earnings, and is not used in this model.
inputs.sbc_note: Immaterial to a bank ROE/book-value model; not separately adjusted.

tsb_deal.synergy_haircut_applied_base_case: 60-70% of guided $34m, phased in FY29-FY31 rather than immediately, reflecting the AU-ADI integration precedent

inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Base case: +200m shares issued at TSB completion (start of FY27) plus a modest ~0.3%/yr ongoing DRP dilution thereafter. Bull case: no ongoing dilution beyond the TSB raise (DRP take-up offset by capital efficiency). Bear case: ~1%/yr ongoing dilution reflecting continued capital strain.

cost_of_equity.coe_rationale: Built up from a CAPM base plus two explicit qualitative premiums specific to Heartland's current situation. (1) NZ risk-free rate ~4.5% + equity risk premium ~6.0% x beta 1.1 = CAPM base 11.1%. (2) +1.0pp small-cap/illiquidity premium (market cap approximately NZ$1.1-1.3bn at the current quote -- larger and more liquid than a true micro-cap, but still well below the trans-Tasman majors, warranting a modest premium rather than the 2%+ used for true micro-caps elsewhere in this repo). (3) +1.0pp dual-regulator/integration-execution premium: Heartland is running the Australian ADI integration (not complete until FY2028) and the TSB Bank merger (targeted December 2026) simultaneously, and must maintain separate RBNZ and APRA capital/risk/compliance infrastructure on an ongoing basis. Total base-case CoE: 13.1%. Bull case lowers CoE to 12.1% (integration risk resolving cleanly reduces the execution premium). Bear case raises CoE to 14.5% (both integrations struggling simultaneously, credit-cycle stress, raises the execution and credit premiums).

historical_growth.eps_note: EPS derived as NetIncome / period-end SharesOutstanding (both millions, from the CSV) x 100 for cents, NOT the CSV's eps column, which is already reported in cents but computed on weighted-average shares -- both methods agree closely where cross-checked (e.g. FY2022: 16.13c either way).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: sustainable_growth_roe_x_retention -- steady-state base-case ROE (~8.5%, FY29-30 average) x (1 - 55% payout ratio) = 3.8% per year. This is the maximum book-value growth rate the base case assumes is financeable from retained earnings once the TSB integration costs are behind the group; it is deliberately NOT the historical equity CAGR (14.7% 3yr), which was earned almost entirely via dilutive capital raises (April 2024 AU-ADI raise; the coming ~$250m TSB raise) rather than retained-earnings compounding.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: SEVERE divergence and the central fact of this valuation: equity 3yr CAGR is +14.66% (capital-raise-driven) while NPAT 3yr CAGR is -25.84% and EPS 3yr CAGR is -36.52% over the SAME period (FY2022-FY2025). A rapidly growing book value is not translating into proportionate profit or per-share earnings growth -- the opposite: per-share earnings power has been destroyed by dilutive raises funding a business earning sub-cost-of-equity returns. This divergence is exactly why the equity/book-value CAGR must NOT be used as a forward earnings-growth proxy here; the model instead derives forward growth from the sustainable-growth formula on projected ROE, and 1H2026's recovery to 7.3% underlying ROE is treated as the start of a partial, not complete, recovery.

base.rationale: FY27-FY28 underlying ROE dips to 6.5-7.0% as TSB integration costs land on top of a still-not-fully-bedded-down Australian ADI integration -- directly echoing the FY2025 reset pattern that followed the April-2024 AU acquisition (two years of sub-8% ROE). From FY29 onward, ROE recovers gradually to 8.5-9.0% by FY31 as roughly 60-70% of the guided $34m TSB synergies are realised, later than management's timeline. Payout stays near the 50-55% policy floor through the raise/integration period given capital retention needs, normalizing toward the group's historical ~55-80% range once integration capital needs ease. Exit at 0.95x book -- a modest re-rating from the current ~0.88x multiple, reflecting a partial but incomplete ROE recovery still below cost of equity by Year 5.

bull.rationale: TSB merger executes cleanly on management's own guidance: $34m of annual synergies fully realised by FY29, >20% year-one EPS accretion materialises roughly as guided, and the combined NZ$15bn-asset 'TSB Heartland Bank' achieves the scale to meaningfully lower its cost-to-income ratio. Underlying ROE recovers to 11% by FY31 -- still below the (lower, bull-case) 12.1% cost of equity, so this is a genuine but not heroic recovery, not a re-rating to cost-of-equity parity. No further ongoing dilution beyond the TSB raise (DRP take-up offset by capital efficiency from the RBNZ's December-2025 capital-settings relief). Exit at 1.10x book reflects the market beginning to price in a durable, scale-driven earnings recovery.

bear.rationale: TSB integration repeats the Australian experience but worse: two simultaneous, unfinished integration programmes (AU technology build not complete until FY2028; TSB systems/culture merger) strain management bandwidth, guided synergies underdeliver materially and land later than even the base case assumes, and Motor/Business Finance credit costs resurface in a softer NZ/AU credit cycle. Underlying ROE stalls at 6-6.5% throughout the horizon, never durably clearing even the FY2026 guidance floor on a sustained basis. Ongoing ~1%/yr dilution reflects continued capital strain requiring further DRP-driven equity issuance. Exit at 0.70x book, a de-rating from the current ~0.88x multiple, reflecting a market that has lost confidence in the TSB thesis.

justified_pb_check.note: This formula-based fair P/B (0.50x, ~NZ$0.69/share, using a steady-state ~8.5% ROE) sits BELOW both the current traded multiple (~0.88x, $1.205 vs H1-2026 BVPS $1.3705) and this model's DCF-style base-case output (0.74x implied against the current BVPS). The gap between the formula-fair price ($0.69) and the current market price ($1.205) is explained by the market pricing in a more optimistic TSB synergy realisation and ROE-recovery path than either the formula (which assumes ROE/CoE persist in perpetuity with zero mean reversion) or this model's finite 5-year base case assumes. The DCF-style base case, unlike the pure formula, gives credit for a FINITE horizon with an assumed partial re-rating exit multiple (0.95x, close to today's) rather than capitalising the depressed near-term ROE in perpetuity -- which is why it lands modestly above the pure formula-fair price ($1.0154 vs $0.691) but still below the current $1.205 quote.

entry_price.methodology: Entry = PV(base-scenario DPS Years 1-5, discounted at 15%) + PV(base-scenario Year-5 exit value at the CoE-derived fair exit price, discounted at 15%). Note the 15% hurdle EXCEEDS the base-case cost of equity (13.1%), so discounting the same exit value at the higher 15% rate mechanically produces a LOWER present value than the CoE-discounted intrinsic value above -- entry price sits below base-case IV, the correct and expected result whenever the hurdle rate exceeds CoE.

base.note: Entry price (NZ$0.94) is well below the current NZ$1.205 quote and below this model's CoE-discounted base intrinsic value (NZ$1.0154) -- an internally consistent result of the 15% IRR hurdle exceeding the 13.1% cost of equity used elsewhere in this model. A buyer paying NZ$0.94 today and exiting at the base-case Year-5 value of NZ$1.5047/share (0.95x projected book) while collecting the projected dividend stream earns approximately a 15% annualised return.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = Cost of Equity (CoE, +/-2pp around the base 13.1%), Columns = Exit Price-to-Book multiple (+/-0.15x/0.30x steps around the base 0.95x) -- the correct second axis for a bank book-value model, in place of WACC/terminal-growth for an FCF DCF. Matrix computed on the BASE-case ROE/payout/book-value/share-count path over 5 years (FY27-FY31).

probability_weighted.note: Bear weighted slightly above the standard 25% (at 30%) and base slightly reduced (45%) because the TSB merger stacks a second, larger integration on top of an Australian ADI integration that produced two years of sub-8% ROE and a genuine FY2025 credit-quality reset -- this is not a hypothetical tail risk but a repeat of a pattern already observed in this company's recent history. Bull is held at a standard 25% because 1H2026's sharp recovery (underlying ROE 7.3%, +540bps YoY) shows the operational turnaround is real and already partly de-risks a clean-execution outcome. The probability-weighted intrinsic value of NZ$0.9792 implies roughly 19% downside to the current NZ$1.205 quote.

income_framing.note: Given the base case's negative price return, the investment case for HGH.NZ at NZ$1.205 depends heavily on whether the TSB merger executes closer to management's guidance (bull case, +7.3%) or repeats the AU integration pattern (base/bear, -16% to -45%). Heartland's stated dividend policy is a floor of >=50% of underlying NPAT; FY2025 total dividend was 4.0cps (80% payout, reflecting the reset year's depressed earnings base), and the 1H2026 interim was 3.5cps (72% payout, up from 2.0cps in 1H2025). Base-case projected DPS over FY27-FY31 ranges from 4.5c to 7.5c, a gross yield of roughly 3.7-6.3% on the current $1.205 price -- but capital is likely to be retained near-term to support the TSB transaction and its integration, and the payout ratio may compress toward the 50% policy floor in FY27-FY28 before normalising. This is a turnaround/M&A-integration story, not a stable income holding, until the TSB merger outcome is clearer (expected to complete December 2026, with FY2026 full-year results due 20 August 2026 -- after this report's data cut-off).

sanity_check.sbc_note: Not separately adjusted; immaterial to a bank ROE/book-value model (see valuation_philosophy.sbc_treatment).

implied_multiples.pb_note: Current price $1.205 / H1-2026 (31-Dec-2025) BVPS $1.3705 (equity $1,289.0m / FY2025 period-end shares 940.559m, the latest confirmed share count) = 0.879x book.
implied_multiples.ev_ebitda_note: Not meaningful for a deposit-funded bank; not computed.

historical_pb_by_fiscal_year_end_june_cl.note: Computed from June-month-end Yahoo closes matched to 30-June fiscal year ends, against period-end shareholders' equity / period-end shares outstanding from the CSV (shares only available from FY2021 onward). FY2018-FY2020 P/B could not be computed (period-end share counts not disclosed pre-FY2021 in the parsed data) but are not needed for the recency-weighted check below.
historical_pb_by_fiscal_year_end_june_cl.10yr_range_available: FY2021-FY2025 (5 fiscal years of usable data): range 0.62x (FY2025 trough, post-reset) to 1.58x (FY2021, pre-AU-acquisition, rate-cycle-driven premium). Heartland has clearly de-rated from a premium-to-book multiple (1.2-1.6x, FY2021-2023) to a discount-to-book multiple (0.6-0.9x, FY2024-2026) coinciding with the April-2024 AU acquisition, subsequent dilutive raise, and the FY2025 credit-quality reset -- consistent with the ROE decline documented in historical_growth and valuation_philosophy.
historical_pb_by_fiscal_year_end_june_cl.current_vs_range: Current implied P/B (0.879x) sits within the recent FY2024-2026 discount-to-book range (0.62x-0.88x-ish, current trading near the top of that recent range) and well below the FY2021-2023 premium era. It is NOT trading in the upper half of the full 5-year range on a like-for-like basis once the structural de-rating is accounted for -- it is near the top of the POST-reset range, i.e. the market has already priced in a partial recovery.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base-case implied P/B of intrinsic value (0.741x) is BELOW both the current traded multiple (0.879x) and the pure justified-P/B formula fair value (0.504x sits below the DCF-style base case, as expected for a finite-horizon model with a re-rating exit multiple) -- the model does not require multiple expansion beyond current trading levels to produce its (negative) base-case output; if anything the base case implies a further modest de-rating from today's multiple is warranted given the TSB integration risk. Base-case upside is negative (-15.7%), so the 'price in upper half of historical range with positive model upside' trip condition is moot by construction. The bull case (+7.3% upside, exit P/B 1.10x) sits within the stock's own historically observed range (up to 1.58x in FY2021) and is not an extrapolation beyond history.
sanity_check.methodology_note: A book-value-compounding model with an exit P/B anchored to the stock's OWN observed post-reset trading range (0.70x-1.10x across scenarios, versus a 5-year historical range of 0.62x-1.58x) was used from the outset, which structurally prevents the peak-earnings extrapolation failure mode this check targets.
